# flatcor

Objective Bayes factors and estimation for linear regression, with priors
that extend Jeffreys' flat correlation to several predictors.

With one predictor, the natural objective prior is flat on the correlation.
With several, not every correlation-based quantity can be flat at once, so
the package offers four priors. One gives each partial correlation its own flat
prior; the other three are one family, *R*² ~ Beta(*a*, 1) with a uniform direction:

| `prior =`                    | *R*² prior    | Kept flat as predictors are added                          |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"independent_partial_r"`  | whatever the partial correlations imply | each partial correlation, on its own (not linked to the others) |
| `"joint_partial_r"` (default) | Beta(*k*/2, 1) | each partial correlation (LKJ(1); `stan_lm` with η = 1) |
| `"flat_r"`                   | Beta(½, 1)      | the multiple correlation *R*                             |
| `"flat_r_squared"`           | Beta(1, 1)       | *R*²                                                    |

One Stan model does everything, for all four priors: the posterior for
estimation, and the Bayes factor between any two linear models, from each
model's marginal likelihood estimated by bridge sampling
([bridgesampling](https://cran.r-project.org/package=bridgesampling)). The
default is joint flat partial r. The validation of the priors side by side
is in [dm-k1/flatcor-simulation-studies](https://github.com/dm-k1/flatcor-simulation-studies);
the argument for them, and the paper, in
[dm-k1/flatcor-paper](https://github.com/dm-k1/flatcor-paper).

## Install

```r
remotes::install_github("dm-k1/flatcor")
```

Everything needs Stan. There are two backends:

- [cmdstanr](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/) with CmdStan installed (the
  default whenever CmdStan is found; the validation used it). Its Bayes
  factors take the model's log density from
  [BridgeStan](https://roualdes.github.io/bridgestan/), so they also need the
  bridgestan package:
  `install.packages("bridgestan", repos = "https://r-multiverse.r-universe.dev")`.
  The first build downloads BridgeStan's C++ sources to `~/.bridgestan`.
- rstan (the fallback when CmdStan is not installed, or with
  `backend = "rstan"`), which installs from CRAN without a separate CmdStan
  and needs no BridgeStan.

Use one of the two per R session: once rstan is loaded, cmdstanr cannot
compute Bayes factors in that session.

## Use

```{r quick-start, eval = FALSE, code = readLines("inst/examples/quick_start.R")[-(1:2)]}
```

A Bayes factor is an estimate with a Monte Carlo error, which is printed with
it (bridgesampling's approximate error of the log Bayes factor). That error
can be optimistic; running again with other seeds shows the spread directly.
Following the bridgesampling authors, each model gets ten times the draws used
for estimation, and models up to about 90 predictors stay within the sizes
they have shown it to work for.

Without `prior =` the functions use joint flat partial r and say so once per
session. Rows with a missing value in a variable of the formula are left out,
with a warning that gives the sample size used. A worked example on one
dataset, start to finish: `system.file("examples", "example.R", package = "flatcor")`.

## Results, builds and parallel work

Nothing flatcor computes is thrown away. `fit_regression()` returns, besides
the draws, the backend's fit, the sampler's diagnostics per chain, the
seconds, the seed and the data Stan got. `bayes_factor_models()` returns the
Bayes factor, its log and error, and per model (`$models$a`, `$models$b`) the
log marginal likelihood, bridge sampling's details, the sampler's diagnostics
and a summary of every Stan variable; `keep_fits = TRUE` also keeps the Stan
fits. See the help pages for the full lists.

The Stan model (`flatcor_model()`) and its log density (`flatcor_density()`)
are built once and kept as files in a cache folder, one per flatcor version
(`options(flatcor.cache = )` or `cache =` chooses it), so every later R
session or process finds them. For parallel workers, build both first and let
the workers share the cache:

```r
options(flatcor.cache = "path/to/cache")
flatcor_model()
flatcor_density()   # cmdstanr only
```

With cmdstanr, each fit's temporary files are deleted once it is read into
memory.
